LUNAVISTA – Lunar Landing Site NavigatorLUNAVISTA – Lunar Landing Site Navigator

LUNAVISTA is an interactive lunar mission-planning and landing-site assessment platform designed to support the identification and evaluation of potential lunar landing regions, particularly near the lunar south pole. It integrates NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) and Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) terrain data with JPL SPICE ephemerides to provide terrain visualization, elevation and slope assessment, 360° horizon analysis, and time-dependent Sun and Earth visibility calculations.

The platform allows users to explore lunar terrain in 2D and 3D, evaluate candidate landing locations, assess illumination and communication line-of-sight opportunities, and compare mission scenarios against defined engineering requirements. Its mission-planning tools also aim to identify suitable mission windows by evaluating actual celestial geometry and terrain constraints over time.

By combining terrain analysis, orbital geometry, visibility modelling, and mission decision support in one platform, LUNAVISTA aims to make lunar landing-site evaluation more accessible, transparent, and data-driven, helping future lunar exploration missions make better-informed decisions.

LUNAVISTA – Lunar Landing Site Navigator

Website URL

1. Project Overview

LUNAVISTA is an interactive lunar terrain exploration, landing-site assessment and mission-planning platform designed to support future lunar exploration, particularly missions targeting the Moon's south polar region.

Selecting a suitable lunar landing site is challenging because the terrain is uneven, sunlight conditions vary significantly over time, and communication opportunities depend on the visibility of Earth. LUNAVISTA addresses these challenges by integrating lunar terrain data, celestial ephemerides, terrain-aware visibility analysis and mission decision-support tools into a unified platform.

2. How It Works

LUNAVISTA combines several scientific and computational systems:

Lunar Terrain Exploration: The platform processes NASA Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) digital elevation models to generate interactive 2D and 3D terrain visualizations. Users can explore surface elevation, slope, terrain profiles and local topography.

Terrain and Landing Assessment: Users can define candidate landing locations and evaluate their surrounding footprints using elevation and slope measurements. The system checks engineering requirements and identifies compliant, non-compliant and indeterminate conditions based on available data.

Celestial Ephemeris: Using NASA/JPL SPICE and the DE421 planetary ephemeris, LUNAVISTA calculates the apparent positions and directions of the Sun and Earth relative to selected lunar surface locations.

Terrain-Aware Visibility: By combining celestial positions with calculated terrain horizons and finite-disk visibility geometry, the platform evaluates solar illumination opportunities and geometric Earth visibility. It calculates full, partial and obstructed visibility periods over selected time intervals.

Mission Planning and Comparison: Users can create mission profiles, define engineering constraints, screen candidate regions, compare alternatives and evaluate possible mission windows using calculated terrain and visibility metrics.

3. Technologies and Tools

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript and Vite.
  • 3D Visualization: Three.js, React Three Fiber and Drei.
  • 2D Mapping: OpenLayers.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Scientific Computing: NumPy, SciPy, Rasterio, GDAL and PyProj.
  • Celestial Mechanics: NAIF SPICE Toolkit and JPL DE421.
  • Data Sources: NASA LOLA elevation products, Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter datasets and NASA lunar mapping resources.

4. Innovation and Creativity

The key innovation of LUNAVISTA is the integration of multiple lunar mission-planning capabilities into a single interactive environment.

Rather than evaluating terrain, sunlight and Earth visibility independently, the platform connects these calculations to support location-specific and time-dependent mission assessment. Its finite solar and Earth disk visibility modelling accounts for terrain obstruction beyond simple horizon or central-body visibility checks.

The mission decision-support system also distinguishes hard engineering constraints from soft preferences, handles incomplete measurements explicitly and avoids treating unavailable scientific data as zero or as a successful result.

5. Benefits and Expected Impact

LUNAVISTA aims to make lunar landing-site exploration more accessible, reproducible and data-driven. It can help researchers, students and mission planners investigate candidate locations, understand terrain-related risks, evaluate illumination and communication opportunities, and compare potential mission windows.

By bringing terrain analysis, celestial geometry and mission planning together, LUNAVISTA provides a foundation for more informed lunar exploration decisions, particularly in the scientifically challenging south polar environment.

6. Design Considerations

The platform is designed around scientific traceability, data provenance, coordinate-system consistency and transparent uncertainty handling. It distinguishes geometric visibility from actual electrical power generation and radio communication performance. It also accounts for limitations in DEM coverage and ephemeris data rather than presenting unsupported measurements as verified results.
